meta.name: Shadow Corner — Dream Pop / Trip-Hop / Dark Jazz Hybrid
meta.description: Trip-hop is the rhythmic and production foundation; dream pop shapes the melodic language and harmonic familiarity; dark jazz is expressed through the instrumental voices and phrasing: tenor sax lead, Rhodes piano, and vibraphone. Intimate, nocturnal, hazy, melancholic, and memorable.
meta.note: Las secciones suman 88 compases (aprox. 4:05.6 a 86 BPM en 4/4). La duración se conserva deliberadamente para este experimento; no acortar ni reestructurar sin autorización.
meta.upgrade_note: Rebuilt as a deliberate hybrid. Trip-hop remains the engine (laid-back breakbeat, deep bass, dusty texture and restrained groove). Dream pop becomes the melodic/harmonic identity (singable sustained phrases, open chords, soft emotional lift, recurring motifs). Dark jazz is the instrumental character rather than the harmonic genre: tenor sax is the lead voice, Rhodes supplies the harmonic bed, and vibraphone adds sparse luminous responses.

global.mode: D Aeolian / natural minor as the emotional center, with F major as its relative-major source for dream-pop lift. Core notes: D E F G A Bb C. Use occasional E natural and C natural as stable color tones; avoid making the harmony sound like a jazz-standard progression.

tracks.name: Atmospheric pad (dream-pop haze)
tracks.role: Wide, soft, blurred background. Long root/fifth or root/octave tones; never compete with sax. Slow attacks and long releases should be implemented by the renderer if available.

tracks.name: Deep bass (trip-hop foundation)
tracks.role: Round, dark, centered low end. Mostly root notes with occasional fifth or octave movement. Sub-heavy but controlled; do not turn the whole mix into a constant 808 wall.

tracks.name: Lead tenor saxophone (dark-jazz voice)
tracks.role: Main melodic identity. Warm, breathy, intimate tenor register; long notes, soft attacks, slight scoops and falls only at phrase endings. Do not write bebop runs or constant improvisation. The melody must remain singable and dream-pop familiar.

tracks.name: Rhodes electric piano (harmonic bed)
tracks.role: Primary chord color and pulse. Soft, rounded Rhodes voicings with 7ths/9ths used sparingly. Broken chords or gently repeated chord tones; avoid bright funk comping and dense jazz voicings.

tracks.name: Vibraphone (dreamlike dark-jazz accents)
tracks.role: Sparse high-register replies, two- or three-note fragments, and occasional sustained color tones. It should answer the sax or leave a small glint between phrases; never double every sax note.

tracks.name: Drums (dusty trip-hop breakbeat)

humanization.hats: irregular low-velocity 16ths; jitter +-10 ticks; omit 25-35%; occasional late hat

tracks.role: The track must still feel like trip-hop first: slow, heavy, swung/laid-back breakbeat, dry snare, restrained kick syncopation, dusty hats. No four-on-the-floor, no busy trap rolls, no rock backbeat.

harmony.harmonic_rhythm: One chord every 2 bars. Keep the progression emotionally clear and loopable; do not add chord changes merely to make the harmony more sophisticated.

voicings.rhodes: Use compact, warm voicings in the middle register. Favor rootless color tones only when the bass clearly supplies the root. Keep 3rds and 7ths audible enough to define the chord; add 9ths as soft color.
voicings.pad: Long root/fifth or root/octave tones, very low in the mix. Avoid semitone clusters as a default.
voicings.vibraphone: Use isolated 9ths, 6ths, fifths, or short chord fragments in the upper register. Leave space around the sax.
voicings.voice_leading: Prefer common tones and small movements. Let the harmony feel like a familiar dream-pop cycle, not a sequence of unrelated jazz substitutions.

tension: Use occasional suspended/add9 color rather than constant dissonance.
A single chromatic approach note may lead into a sax target at a phrase boundary, but the main melody should stay inside D natural minor / F major.
Create emotional tension through sustained notes over changing chords, delayed resolution, and arrangement space.
harmony.harmonic_intent: The relative-major colors (F, Bb, C) provide the familiar, floating dream-pop surface, while D minor remains the emotional center. Dark jazz should come from sax tone, Rhodes voicings, vibraphone resonance, phrasing, and space—not from making every chord harmonically obscure.

sections.name: intro
sections.notes: Atmospheric opening: Rhodes establishes the chord color; pad is soft and wide; one or two vibraphone notes leave long tails. No drums or bass until the groove enters.

sections.name: verse_1
sections.strings: full en el 1er loop, bare en el 2o
sections.notes: Trip-hop pocket stays restrained. Sax phrases are sparse and vocal-like; Rhodes holds warm chord shapes; vibraphone answers only in phrase gaps.

sections.name: bridge
sections.notes: Strip back the beat. Expose the sax over Rhodes; vibraphone offers isolated replies. Avoid jazz soloing.

sections.name: chorus
sections.notes: Main dream-pop lift over the same trip-hop foundation. Sax hook is clear and repeatable; vibraphone adds only selected high notes.

sections.name: verse_2
sections.notes: Return to lower energy. Preserve the groove and introduce a small sax phrase variation; keep the same harmonic familiarity.

sections.name: final_chorus
sections.notes: C2 then C1. Emotional peak comes from width, sustain and motif recognition, not extra notes or a louder sax solo.

sections.name: outro
sections.notes: Drums fade first; sax gives one final short statement; Rhodes and vibraphone tails dissolve into the pad.

melody.principle: Dream-pop melodic language performed by a dark, breathy tenor sax: memorable stepwise shapes, small leaps, sustained notes, clear rests, and repeated motifs. Avoid bebop vocabulary, virtuosic runs, excessive chromaticism, and constant fills. The sax should feel like a human voice.

layout.verse: Sparse sax phrase A in first 8 bars; phrase B in second 8 bars with a slightly higher emotional peak.
layout.chorus: C1 is the main 8-bar hook; C2 is a related 8-bar variation. Repeat with small arrangement changes, not a new melody.
layout.chorus_final: Play C2 then C1. The final C1 should feel like recognition and emotional return, not a bigger jazz solo.

bends.sax_scoop: Optional subtle approach from approximately -0.2 semitone to target over 100-140 ticks; only on selected phrase entries.
bends.sax_fall: Optional fall of approximately -0.2 semitone near the end of selected sustained notes; never on every note.
bends.implementation_warning: Pitch bend is channel-wide in MIDI. Use a dedicated sax channel and configure the bend range before applying bends. If the renderer cannot support this safely, omit bends rather than affecting other tracks.

bass.pattern: Deep, restrained trip-hop bass. Long root notes with occasional fifth or octave pickup; main attacks on beat 1 and selected offbeat anticipations around beat 3.5. Leave gaps for kick.
bass.outro: One long root note per bar, gradually reducing velocity.
bass.bridge: One long note every 2 bars; allow the bridge to breathe.
bass.sound_note: Prioritize low fundamental and controlled sub energy. Avoid bright plucked bass attack or constant 808 slides.

drums.verse: Half-time trip-hop pocket. Kick on beat 1 with occasional syncopated ghost kick; snare on beat 3, slightly late; sparse closed hats with uneven velocity and omissions.
drums.pre_chorus: Reduce hat density and simplify kick; create anticipation through space, not a drum fill.
drums.bridge: Kick on 1, rim/snare on 3 every other bar, occasional soft hat. Keep the sax exposed.
drums.chorus: Slightly fuller breakbeat: alternate syncopated kicks, dry snare on 3, restrained clap layer, subtle open-hat accents. Preserve the laid-back trip-hop swing; do not turn it into dance pop.
drums.outro: Kick and snare disappear over the first 3 bars; leave pad, Rhodes tail, and room texture.

rhythm.groove_identity: The listener should identify the track as trip-hop from the pocket, bass/drum relationship, dusty transients, and negative space—even when the melody and chords lean dream pop.

dynamics.range: General velocities 48-82; chorus peaks around 88-90. Avoid constant maximum intensity.
dynamics.pad: Very low in intro and verses; widen gradually in chorus without masking the sax.
dynamics.sax: Lead is clear but not loud or aggressive. Verse intimate; chorus slightly more open; bridge exposed and restrained.
dynamics.rhodes: Warm midrange support. Avoid excessive velocity that creates a bright, percussive attack.
dynamics.vibraphone: Sparse, low-velocity accents; let reverb tails overlap naturally but do not create continuous shimmer.
dynamics.fade: Outro velocities taper from approximately 60 to 18. Long audio fade can be applied by the renderer.
dynamics.humanization: Small timing offsets and velocity variation. Keep sax phrasing intentional; humanization must not destabilize the groove.

mp3_render.synth: FluidSynth + GeneralUser-GS.sf2 (or another verified GM soundfont)
extras: Soft vinyl crackle and tape hiss, subtle and mostly in intro/outro
Low-pass around 8-9 kHz as a starting point; preserve sax presence and vibraphone definition
Moderate room/plate reverb on sax; long diffuse reverb on pad and vibraphone; short/dry room on drums
Rhodes with gentle chorus or stereo modulation if available; keep low end mono
Loudness target around -18 LUFS integrated for reference preview; do not hard-limit the transients
Optional 18-22 second exponential fade at the end
mix_priority: 1. Trip-hop groove and bass remain the foundation
2. Tenor sax melody is the recognizable foreground
4. Vibraphone adds selective color and replies
5. Pad and noise create atmosphere without filling every gap

validation.status: Specification updated; generated MIDI must be validated after Claude renders it.

claude_generation_brief.purpose: Generate a MIDI and preview rendering for a hybrid composition where trip-hop is the base, dream pop shapes the melodic/harmonic language, and dark jazz supplies the instrumental character.
priority_order: 1. Preserve a convincing laid-back trip-hop drum/bass pocket.
2. Make the tenor sax hook memorable, lyrical, spacious, and familiar in a dream-pop sense.
3. Use Rhodes as the main harmonic instrument with open, warm chord voicings.
4. Use vibraphone sparingly for high-register responses and color.
5. Keep the atmosphere dark, hazy, intimate, and restrained.
must_do: Use the tenor sax track as the sole primary lead melody.
Use the active chorus_hook_c1 and chorus_hook_c2 phrases as the main chorus material.
Treat sax phrases as monophonic; do not overlap notes unless an intentional legato overlap is needed.
Use Rhodes for chord voicings and gentle broken-chord motion; do not make it a busy jazz comping track.
Use vibraphone as a sparse secondary voice, mainly in gaps between sax phrases.
Keep the trip-hop groove slow, heavy, swung/laid-back, and slightly dusty.
Preserve the 88-bar arrangement and the 4/4 meter.
Respect the specified pitch ranges, channel assignments, and note durations.
If GM program numbering is zero-based in the MIDI library, use the exact program values supplied in tracks.
creative_freedom: You may add a few Rhodes chord tones or vibraphone replies where the arrangement explicitly leaves space.
You may make subtle voicing inversions to improve voice leading.
You may vary drum ghost notes between repeated sections while preserving the pocket.
You may use small sax articulations and phrase-end bends if MIDI implementation supports them correctly.
do_not: Do not turn the track into straight dream pop, shoegaze, jazz fusion, lounge jazz, or cinematic orchestral music.
Do not write bebop runs, virtuosic sax solos, constant vibraphone arpeggios, or dense Rhodes chords.
Do not replace the trip-hop beat with four-on-the-floor or trap percussion.
Do not make every chord a complex jazz extension; harmonic familiarity is intentional.
Do not add a second competing lead melody.
Do not fill every rest. Silence is part of the arrangement.
Do not use the choir pad as a lead instrument.
Do not use the original baseline hook arrays from earlier versions if they are present; use the active phrases in this file.
deliverables: A short implementation report listing tempo, bars, tracks, program numbers, and any unsupported MIDI/render instructions.

musical_appeal_engine.design_intent: Increase the chance of a memorable and replayable composition through clear melodic identity, a stable groove, harmonic familiarity, and controlled contrast. This is a compositional design heuristic, not a prediction of commercial success.

genre_hierarchy.foundation: Trip-hop: drum pocket, bass weight, dusty production, negative space.
genre_hierarchy.melodic_language: Dream pop: lyrical contour, sustained notes, memorable repetition, floating harmonic color.
genre_hierarchy.instrumental_identity: Dark jazz: tenor sax phrasing, Rhodes warmth, vibraphone resonance and selective improvisational inflection.
genre_hierarchy.rule: The three influences have different jobs. Do not blend them equally in every bar.

principles: A memorable melodic contour is more valuable than note density.
The chorus should be recognizable after one or two listens.
Repeat the central motif before introducing variation.
Use chord color to create emotional lift, not harmonic obscurity.
Let the sax breathe; use vibraphone to answer rather than double it.
Keep the drum/bass relationship stable enough to anchor the hybrid.

hook_architecture.main_motif: A compact rising-and-falling shape built around D-F-E-C colors in D minor.
hook_architecture.c1: Main motif statement and repeat, with long notes and clear rests.
hook_architecture.c2: Related variation that lifts briefly, then resolves toward A/G/F/D-related tones.
hook_architecture.test: Check whether a listener can hum or recognize the contour without hearing the exact soundfont.

arrangement_energy: Intro: establish haze and Rhodes color before the beat arrives.
Verse: low-density groove and intimate sax phrases.
Pre-chorus: create lift by thinning the drums and raising the melodic register slightly.
Chorus: fuller trip-hop pocket, wider pad, and the recurring sax motif.
Bridge: strip back the groove and expose sax/Rhodes/vibraphone interaction.
Outro: remove drums and leave the harmonic atmosphere to decay.

human_evaluation_rubric.scale: 1-5, manually evaluated; do not invent scores.
criteria: Can the listener recognize the sax motif after one pass?
Does the beat still feel unmistakably trip-hop?
Does the melody feel emotionally familiar rather than technically clever?
Does the vibraphone add a memorable color without clutter?
Would the listener replay the chorus?
human_evaluation_rubric.method: Compare this hybrid against the previous Shadow Corner version at matched playback level. Change one major variable per next iteration.

automated_checks: Check sax monophony and note range.
Check no accidental overlaps between sax and vibraphone in the same register.
Check that the chorus motif repeats with consistent rhythm.
Check that bass and kick do not collide excessively.
Check that vibraphone notes are sparse and mostly occur in sax gaps.
Do not claim that automated MIDI checks can measure catchiness.

midi_implementation_notes.beat_indexing: Beat positions are 1-based within each phrase/loop; fractional beats are allowed.
midi_implementation_notes.pitch: pitch is a MIDI note number. Sax melody is written for concert pitch; do not transpose unless the target soundfont/instrument workflow explicitly requires it.
midi_implementation_notes.duration: dur is measured in quarter-note beats.
midi_implementation_notes.channels: MIDI channel values are zero-based in this JSON. Channel 9 is the standard percussion channel (human MIDI channel 10).
midi_implementation_notes.program_numbers: General MIDI program values are zero-based. Tenor Sax=66, Electric Piano 1=4, Vibraphone=11, Synth Bass 1=38, Choir Pad=91.
midi_implementation_notes.pitch_bend: Pitch bend is a 14-bit channel message. Configure bend range via RPN on the sax channel only. Do not share the sax channel with other pitched tracks.
midi_implementation_notes.non_midi_rendering: Reverb character, chorus, tape hiss, vinyl crackle, low-pass filtering, stereo width, loudness and fades are audio-rendering tasks, not ordinary MIDI note events.
midi_implementation_notes.gain: gain and descriptive role fields are renderer metadata, not standard MIDI events.
validation: Confirm six tracks and correct GM programs.
Confirm sax lead notes are monophonic and within range.
Confirm vibraphone is sparse and does not double the sax throughout.
Confirm bass is low enough to provide weight without masking kick.
Confirm all note end times stay within their intended sections.
Confirm tempo and time-signature metadata are written to the MIDI file.
Report unsupported renderer-specific instructions instead of silently ignoring them.
